title: Rise of the Guardians
tagline: The Guardians are coming to dinner.
about: Jack Frost joins Santa, the Easter Bunny, the Tooth Fairy and the Sandman to stop the Bogeyman.
cue: Serve the sweets when the Easter Bunny's egg hunt begins.
faces: North's workshop pelmeni with sour cream

The yetis make the toys, the elves think they doHow to make it250g beef mince250g pork mince1 brown onion1 tsp salt40 round dumpling wrappers40g butter150g sour cream1 bunch dillMix the beef, pork, grated onion, salt and pepper.Put a teaspoon on each wrapper, fold into a half moon, seal and pinch the ends together.Boil in salted water in batches for 5 minutes after they float.Toss with the melted butter and serve with sour cream and chopped dill.Jamie's snow day mac and cheese bitesBurgess, the snowy town where Jamie still believesHow to make it200g macaroni30g butter2 tbsp plain flour400ml full cream milk150g cheddar1 tsp Dijon mustard1 egg30g parmesanCook the macaroni until just tender and drain.Melt the butter, stir in the flour, then whisk in the milk until thick.Off the heat stir in the grated cheddar, mustard, egg and macaroni.Spoon into a greased 24-hole mini muffin tin, top with grated parmesan and bake at 200°C.Cool 10 minutes before lifting out.MainsNorth's beef stroganoff and noodlesRump strips and mushrooms in creamy sauce over egg noodlesHow to make it600g rump steak1 tbsp vegetable oil1 onion300g mushrooms50g butter1 tsp sweet paprika1 tbsp Dijon mustard300ml beef stock200g sour cream400g egg noodles1 bunch of dillSlice the rump into thin strips, the onion and the mushrooms.Sear the beef in batches in a hot pan with oil, then remove.Fry the onion and mushrooms in butter.Add the paprika, Dijon and stock and simmer.Stir in the sour cream and the beef and warm through without boiling.Cook the egg noodles, toss in butter and dill and serve under the beef.Bunnymund's Aussie lamb chops with minted peasBunny's from Down Under, and he won't let you forget itHow to make it8 lamb loin chops2 garlic cloves, crushed2 sprigs of rosemary3 tbsp olive oil800g chat potatoes, halved400g frozen peas1 bunch mint30g butter1 lemonHeat the oven to 220°C. Toss the potatoes with 2 tbsp oil and salt and roast until crisp.Rub the chops with garlic, chopped rosemary and the rest of the oil.Grill the chops on a hot barbecue or pan until charred and pink inside, then rest.Boil the peas, then crush with the butter, chopped mint and a squeeze of lemon.SweetsBunnymund's hot cross bun egg puddingBaked hot cross bun pudding with mini chocolate eggsHow to make it6 hot cross buns30g butter150g mini chocolate eggs3 eggs400ml full cream milk400ml thickened cream60g caster sugar1 tsp vanilla extract1 tbsp icing sugarButter and halve the hot cross buns and lay them in a baking dish, cut-side up and overlapping.Tuck the mini chocolate eggs between them.Whisk the eggs, milk, cream, sugar and vanilla and pour over.Stand for 15 minutes.Bake at 170°C until set and golden.Dust with icing sugar and serve warm with cream and a few more mini eggs.Iced gingerbread yetis and elvesSpiced gingerbread men iced as white-furred yetis and red-hatted elvesHow to make it100g butter100g golden syrup80g brown sugar300g self-raising flour2 tsp ground ginger1 tsp ground cinnamon1 egg200g icing sugar1 bottle of red food colouringMelt the butter with golden syrup and brown sugar.Mix in the flour, ginger, cinnamon and egg.Chill the dough for 30 minutes.Roll to 5mm and cut big gingerbread men for yetis and small ones for elves.Bake at 180°C.Cool completely.Mix the icing sugar with water, pipe shaggy white fur on the yetis and tint a little red for the elves' hats.Sandy's golden dream honeycombCrunchy golden honeycomb dipped in milk chocolateHow to make it200g caster sugar5 tbsp golden syrup2 tsp bicarbonate of soda100g milk chocolate1 jar of edible gold glitterLine a 20cm square tin with baking paper.Heat the sugar and golden syrup in a deep pan, stirring until dissolved.Boil without stirring until deep golden.Take off the heat, quickly whisk in the bicarbonate of soda and pour into the tin without spreading.Set for 1 hour, then break into chunks.Dip half of each chunk in melted milk chocolate and dust with edible gold glitter.DrinksJack Frost's frosty blue slushieIcy blue lime slushie with a sugar rimHow to make it3 limes3 tbsp caster sugar1 bag of ice120ml blue cordial1 bunch of mint600ml lemonadeDip the rims of the glasses in lime juice, then in caster sugar.Freeze the glasses for 10 minutes.Blend the ice with blue cordial, lime juice and mint leaves until slushy.Add the lemonade and pulse twice.Pour into the frosted glasses and garnish with a mint sprig.Sbiten, hot honey and spiceWarms the yetis after Phil's sleigh test.How
